P1.evidence: Frame delivered in substance — 'I just really want to understand you, like where you're at with your fitness right now and what you're looking to accomplish. Maybe what have some of the challenges been. And then from there, if it's something that we can 100% help with, we'll go into all the details' — and it functioned as the open question, launching the prospect straight into his history. No frame-agreement question was asked; 'You ready to jump right in?' came before the frame, not after, so P1c is a miss. P1a N/A: no setter, prospect self-booked after years of following Trevor. Worth noting for coaching rather than scoring: the rep opened a $6,000 conversation with 'Dude, I've got a voice cracked. I may have been out doing stuff I should have been last night.'

P2.evidence: Work was the standout — asked properly and to the right depth: 'What type of work do you do?' then 'Is that like lots of, is that pretty active?' producing ten-hour desk days, 9:30 to 7:30. Training history and honest frequency both asked: 'were you still working out consistently, or did you stop going as much as well over these last five years?' got 'there were times where I didn't go for six months.' Results from current training asked with a genuinely good diagnostic: 'are we talking I'm plateauing because I just haven't changed up my routines at all, or is part of the plateau because maybe the consistency of working out is also not there as much?' Against that: age was asked 28 minutes in and only as an afterthought ('I actually didn't even ask how old are you?'), and height and weight were never established at all on a call sold on fat loss. Health conditions were never asked — the two bulging discs arrived unprompted mid-sentence — though the rep did follow them up well once they landed ('when did the injury happen?'). Diet only got a macro-tracking question, and sleep and energy were never mentioned.

P3.evidence: Surface goals asked cleanly — 'what are we talking here? Goals wise. Do you want to get like a six pack or just what exactly are you looking to achieve?' The why-bridge ran twice and worked: 'is that really the thing that's pushing you to kind of get back into shape again or is there anything else?' followed by 'You said that's part of the reason. Is there any other things going on, on top of that?' produced the family material — 'I have a heavier set family... I don't want to ever get like that' — which is the deepest thing said on the call. And then it was dropped. The biggest-reason question at 00:11:26 got answered with logistics ('I can take the kettlebells... I'm not tied down to a gym') and the rep accepted portability as the why. Nobody was ever named as impacted: the ex-partner, the family he does not want to resemble, and the dating life he is rebuilding all appeared and none became a stake. The reflect-back was about behaviour rather than identity and carried no confirmation question.

P4.evidence: The root-cause question was the best-executed move on the call: 'why do you think it's something where you get back in shape and then fall off?' pushed past 'stupid excuses' to the real answer — 'it's prioritizing my time to make money in my relationship. I felt like those were more important than my own fitness.' Followed sensibly with the structural check 'Has anything changed in your schedule? Are you still working the same 10-hour days?' — answered yes, which is the single most important unresolved risk in the deal and was never pressed. The gap: the prospect had a coach who worked ('that's part of the reason why I got so shredded was he dialed me in so well') and nobody asked what happened to that arrangement or why it ended. P4f is a pointed miss here — this is a man with the knowledge, the macro-tracking habit and a proven coaching relationship, so 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' was the exact question, and it was never asked.

P5.evidence: One partial attempt, aimed at relapse rather than inaction: 'what I don't want to happen is if we say, hey, let's work together, you get great results for six months or a year, and then something changes again. And therefore, you fall back off.' That is a real cost frame and it did useful work, but it is not the phase. No 'what does the next two years look like if nothing changes', no 'are you willing to settle for that', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The prospect had handed over the raw material — a five-year decline, a family he is afraid of resembling, and a cycle he has run three or four times — and none of it was converted into a cost of standing still.

P6.evidence: The only call in this batch where the commitment check ran properly and before the number. The scale question at 00:36:36 — 'on a scale of one to 10, one is like, dude, give me off the phone, this sounds horrible. 10 is like, I can definitely see this helping me and feel like this is what I need' — produced '10, easily. Trust me when I tell you that I'm all in right now, and I'm ready to advance myself.' Price came two minutes later and payment eight minutes after that. P6b is partial only because the isolation question was never actually asked; the prospect volunteered 'I'm all in' rather than being asked whether anything would stop him, so if something had been hiding there was no mechanism to surface it.

P11.evidence: Strongest P11 in the batch. Payment collected live via a link in the Zoom chat and confirmed on screen. Trevor's onboarding call booked on the call for Wednesday at 7:15 with the time-zone difference checked. The agreement email was confirmed as arrived and opened — 'I'm viewing it now. It says I need a sign' — but the rep never came back to confirm he actually signed before hanging up, so step 3 finished unverified. Step 4 half-ran: Skool was screen-shared, the classroom and Thursday 12:30 group workout were walked through, and the onboarding form was pointed at ('just fill out the onboarding form'), but the membership was left 'pending' with the rep messaging the team, and he was never told to complete the questionnaire before the Trevor call.

objection_plays.detail: No stall of any kind — the prospect asked for the price himself twice before it was offered.

No money objection in substance. A payment-mechanics question was asked — 'Is that all paid at one time or is it, can it be like a monthly payment?' — and answered with a credit-card deflection rather than a disclosure that financing exists. The prospect paid in full eight minutes later, so the play was never triggered, but the deflection is logged as a flag because the same rep disclosed financing to other prospects the same week.
Timing was actively in favour — he had been waiting to move to Florida for the weather and the backyard before signing up.
No fear or doubt; he volunteered that posting videos and talking to a coach do not faze him.

notes: Score the process, not the result: this closed because the fit was perfect and the prospect arrived pre-sold after five years of following Trevor, not because the process ran. P6 before the price and a complete P11 are genuinely good and worth holding up as the template. But P5 never ran, the deep-why was abandoned the moment the prospect answered with logistics, and the one structural risk in the deal — ten-hour days that have not changed and have derailed him three times before — was identified, confirmed unchanged, and then never addressed. The urgent item is not coaching: he has two MRI-confirmed bulging discs, nobody asked whether a clinician cleared loaded ballistic work, and he has now paid.
